title: derive MVT matching point
stem: Let f(x)=x^3-3x on [-2,2]. Which set contains every c in (-2,2) guaranteed by the Mean Value Theorem to satisfy f'(c)=[f(2)-f(-2)]/4?

choices.label: A
choices.text: c=0 only
choices.rationale: At c=0 the derivative is -3, not the secant slope 1; the equation has two solutions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: c=-2/sqrt(3) and c=2/sqrt(3)
choices.rationale: Correct: The polynomial meets both hypotheses. f(2)=2 and f(-2)=-2, so the secant slope is 1. Solve 3c²-3=1 to get c²=4/3, hence both interior solutions ±2/sqrt(3).

choices.label: C
choices.text: c=-2 and c=2
choices.rationale: The theorem specifies c strictly inside the interval, and the endpoint derivatives do not equal 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No c exists because f' changes sign on the interval.
choices.rationale: A derivative may change sign while a polynomial remains continuous and differentiable; that does not invalidate MVT.

title: derive MVT matching point (variant 1)
stem: Let g(x)=x^3+2x on [-3,3]. What are all interior c values whose instantaneous slope equals the secant slope over the interval, as MVT guarantees?

choices.label: A
choices.text: c=0 only
choices.rationale: G'(0)=2, which differs from the secant slope 11; two interior points work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: c=-3 and c=3
choices.rationale: Endpoints are excluded by the theorem, and their slopes are 29 rather than 11.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is no such c because g is increasing throughout the interval.
choices.rationale: Increasing functions can still have an instantaneous slope equal to their average slope.

choices.label: D
choices.text: c=-sqrt(3) and c=sqrt(3)
choices.rationale: Correct: The secant slope is (g(3)-g(-3))/6=11. Since g'(x)=3x²+2, solving 3c²+2=11 gives c=±sqrt(3), both interior.

title: derive MVT matching point (variant 2)
stem: A polynomial h(x)=x^3-6x is examined on [-1,3]. Which interior c values make h'(c) equal to its average rate of change on that interval?

choices.label: A
choices.text: c=sqrt(7/3) only
choices.rationale: Correct: h(-1)=5 and h(3)=9, so the secant slope is 1. h'(c)=3c²-6=1 gives c=±sqrt(7/3), but only the positive root lies in (-1,3).

choices.label: B
choices.text: c=-1 and c=3
choices.rationale: The endpoints are excluded and do not solve the derivative equation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: c=1 only
choices.rationale: H'(1)=-3, so the midpoint is not the matching point.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No interior point is required because h has a local maximum.
choices.rationale: A polynomial satisfies MVT even when it has extrema within the interval.

title: derive MVT matching point (variant 3)
stem: For p(x)=x^3 on [0,3], which interior value c has p'(c) equal to the average rate of change from 0 to 3?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: C=3 is an endpoint, excluded by MVT, and p'(3)=27 rather than 9.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: P'(1)=3, which is below the average rate 9.

choices.label: C
choices.text: c=sqrt(3)
choices.rationale: Correct: The secant slope is (27-0)/3=9. Solving 3c²=9 gives c=±sqrt(3), but only +sqrt(3) lies in (0,3).

choices.label: D
choices.text: No c exists because p'(0)=0 differs from the average rate.
choices.rationale: Endpoint derivatives need not equal the secant slope; MVT guarantees an interior equality for this polynomial.

title: check MVT hypotheses
stem: A student applies MVT to f(x)=|x| on [-1,1] and says there must be an interior c with f'(c)=0 because the endpoint values agree. Which response is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MVT applies because f is continuous, and c=0 has derivative 0.
choices.rationale: A cusp has no derivative at 0; continuity alone is insufficient for MVT.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The conclusion is not guaranteed: f is not differentiable at 0, and its derivative is -1 or +1 wherever defined inside.
choices.rationale: Correct: The closed-interval continuity condition holds, but the open-interval differentiability condition fails at the cusp x=0. At other interior points f' is ±1, never 0.

choices.label: C
choices.text: MVT applies because f is differentiable at both endpoints.
choices.rationale: Endpoint differentiability is not the theorem's requirement and does not repair the interior cusp.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every interior point works because the secant slope is 0.
choices.rationale: A zero secant slope does not force each derivative to be zero, and here none is.

title: check MVT hypotheses (variant 1)
stem: For q(x)=sqrt(x) on [0,4], a student rejects MVT because q'(0) is undefined. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MVT applies: differentiability is required on (0,4), not at 0; the secant slope is 1/2 and q'(1)=1/2.
choices.rationale: Correct: sqrt(x) is continuous on [0,4] and differentiable on (0,4). Its secant slope is (2-0)/4=1/2, and 1/(2sqrt(c))=1/2 gives c=1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: MVT fails because the derivative must exist at both endpoints of a closed interval.
choices.rationale: The theorem asks for continuity at endpoints and differentiability only in the open interval.

choices.label: C
choices.text: MVT applies, but the matching derivative occurs only at x=0.
choices.rationale: X=0 is excluded from the sought interior point and has no finite derivative.

choices.label: D
choices.text: MVT fails because the graph is not a straight line.
choices.rationale: MVT applies to nonlinear differentiable curves; the graph need not itself be a straight line.

title: check MVT hypotheses (variant 2)
stem: A student uses MVT on r(x)=1/x over [-1,1], claiming that some interior tangent has slope [r(1)-r(-1)]/2=1. Which objection is decisive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MVT applies because the endpoint values are finite, so a tangent of slope +1 is guaranteed.
choices.rationale: Finite endpoint values do not imply continuity through the interval's interior.

choices.label: B
choices.text: r is undefined at 0, so it is not continuous on [-1,1]; in fact r'(x)=-1/x² never equals +1 where defined.
choices.rationale: Correct: The domain gap at 0 breaks closed-interval continuity and open-interval differentiability. Every defined derivative is negative, while the endpoint secant slope is positive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: MVT fails only because r' is undefined at x=-1 and x=1.
choices.rationale: Endpoint derivative values are not required by MVT; the interior discontinuity is decisive.

choices.label: D
choices.text: MVT applies with c=0 because the two branches are symmetric.
choices.rationale: The function and derivative are undefined at c=0, so symmetry supplies no MVT point.

title: check MVT hypotheses (variant 3)
stem: A student applies MVT to s(x)=x^(2/3) on [-1,1], where both endpoint values equal 1, and concludes s'(c)=0 for some interior c. Which analysis is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cusp at 0 makes s nondifferentiable there; at every other interior x the derivative is nonzero, so MVT does not apply and no such c exists.
choices.rationale: Correct: s is continuous, but s'(x)=(2/3)x^(-1/3) is undefined at 0 and nonzero elsewhere in (-1,1). The differentiability hypothesis fails.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The equal endpoints force c=0 with derivative 0.
choices.rationale: A cusp derivative does not become zero merely because endpoint values match.

choices.label: C
choices.text: MVT applies because s is continuous, regardless of interior differentiability.
choices.rationale: MVT requires differentiability throughout the open interval as well as closed-interval continuity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The theorem guarantees c=-1 or c=1 because both are endpoint extrema.
choices.rationale: The theorem seeks an interior point, not either endpoint.

title: interpret average and instantaneous rate
stem: A differentiable distance function records 0 miles at noon and 150 miles at 3 p.m. It is continuous throughout the trip. A driver claims the instantaneous rate was always below 45 miles per hour. Which statement follows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average rate is 45 miles per hour, so the claim could be correct.
choices.rationale: 150 miles divided by three hours is 50 miles per hour, not 45.

choices.label: B
choices.text: MVT guarantees the rate is 50 miles per hour at every moment of the trip.
choices.rationale: MVT guarantees at least one interior time, not a constant rate at every time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The endpoint data imply an average rate of 50 miles per hour, so MVT guarantees a time strictly between noon and 3 p.m. with instantaneous rate 50; the claim is incompatible.
choices.rationale: Correct: The average rate is (150-0)/3=50. The stated continuity and differentiability imply at least one interior instantaneous rate of 50, contradicting an always-below-45 bound.

choices.label: D
choices.text: MVT cannot apply because the distance at intermediate times is not listed.
choices.rationale: An explicit formula or intermediate observations are unnecessary when the hypotheses and endpoints are known.

title: interpret average and instantaneous rate (variant 1)
stem: A tank's water volume rises from 20 to 68 liters over four minutes. Volume is continuous over the closed interval and differentiable inside. An observer says inflow was always under 10 liters per minute. What does MVT imply?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An interior instant has rate 10 liters per minute, confirming the claim.
choices.rationale: The 48-liter increase over four minutes yields 12, not 10.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The volume must rise at 12 liters per minute during every minute.
choices.rationale: MVT supplies at least one instant, not a constant rate over the full interval.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only endpoint rates can be inferred, so the claim cannot be evaluated.
choices.rationale: The theorem yields an interior rate from endpoints and regularity, not an endpoint derivative.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An interior instant has volume-change rate 12 liters per minute, contradicting the claimed upper bound.
choices.rationale: Correct: The average change is (68-20)/4=12 liters per minute; MVT guarantees an interior derivative of 12, which exceeds the claimed upper bound 10.

title: interpret average and instantaneous rate (variant 2)
stem: A continuously differentiable cooling object's temperature falls from 80 to 56 degrees over six minutes. A sensor report claims its temperature-change rate was always greater than -3 degrees per minute. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MVT gives +4 degrees per minute because temperature is positive.
choices.rationale: The signed rate is negative because temperature decreased, despite positive temperature values.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The report is consistent because -4 is greater than -3.
choices.rationale: On the number line -4 is less than -3, contradicting an always-greater-than--3 report.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The rate must have been exactly -4 throughout the six minutes.
choices.rationale: MVT guarantees one matching instant, not a constant rate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: MVT guarantees an interior temperature-change rate of -4 degrees per minute, so the report is inconsistent.
choices.rationale: Correct: The average change is (56-80)/6=-4 degrees per minute. At some interior time the instantaneous derivative equals -4, which is not greater than -3.

title: interpret average and instantaneous rate (variant 3)
stem: A plant's measured height increases from 8 to 23 centimeters in five days. Assume height is continuous and differentiable on the required intervals. Which claim is guaranteed by MVT, and which is not?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The growth rate equals 3 centimeters per day on every day.
choices.rationale: An average rate does not imply the same instantaneous rate throughout the interval.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The growth rate equals 15 centimeters per day at the fifth-day endpoint.
choices.rationale: The total increase is 15 centimeters, not a per-day rate, and an endpoint derivative is not guaranteed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least one interior instant has growth rate 3 centimeters per day; the theorem does not say when or that the rate stays 3.
choices.rationale: Correct: The secant slope is (23-8)/5=3 centimeters per day. MVT guarantees at least one interior derivative equal to that average, without fixing its time or constancy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No instantaneous rate can be inferred without knowing the formula for height.
choices.rationale: MVT needs endpoints and its regularity hypotheses, not an explicit height formula.
